failure.heading: 16. A session stopped placing its messages once the window said nothing moved — 2026-10-03

observed_failure.description: An independently prompted work turn has no placement call in its public action span before the reply. The hook still gives an unchanged window.

events.text:
The "merged rows" were a damaged line in the queue table in [docs/tickets/README.md](docs/tickets/README.md). Each ticket is one table row, and each row must sit on its own line.

During the `.0017` close, I deleted `.0017`'s row with an edit, and two neighbouring rows ended up on a single line:

```
| [A question that keeps coming back rises](…) | Planned … | AFK | A held question … rewrites the store. || [The tickets' open issues are entries of the store](…) | Planned | HITL | Every open issue … |
```

The `||` in the middle is where the `.0015` row ended and the `.0020` row began without a line break. Rendered as markdown, that's one row with too many cells. The `.0020` ticket ("The tickets' open issues are entries of the store") effectively disappeared from the queue, even though its file was fine.

I noticed it during `.0011`'s close and split the line back into two rows. It was my edit's doing, though I can't say exactly how a single row deletion took the line break with it. This time I deleted the row together with its line ending and ran a quick check that every row is whole.

**Why I raised it:** `tickets.py --check` passed both times with the broken line in place. It checks that ticket files and queue rows agree in some respects, but not that every row is a single well-formed line with the right number of cells. So nothing would have caught it if I hadn't happened to read that line.

That's the gap I was asking about. Small, but it's the queue that every session's `/recall` reads. Do you want a ticket for it, a note on the ticket mechanism's open issues, or leave it?
